title: Wake up 1 hour earlier
description: The morning belongs to you before it belongs to the world. Wake up an hour earlier and use that time just for yourself.
proof_prompt: Write what you did in that hour and how you felt.
steps: Set your alarm 1h earlier
Resist the urge to sleep in
Do something just for you in that hour
reflection: What did you discover about yourself in the quiet of the morning?

title: 24h without social media
description: A whole day without scrolling. Notice what shows up when you're no longer distracted.
proof_prompt: Screenshot of Screen Time showing 0 minutes.
steps: Temporarily delete the apps
Let your friends know you're offline
Notice what you feel when you get the urge to open your phone
reflection: What did you do with the time you gained?

title: 7 days of exercise in a row
description: 20 minutes of movement a day, 7 days straight. Any kind counts.
proof_prompt: Photo or screenshot from your fitness app on day 7.
steps: Pick an activity you enjoy
Schedule it firmly in your calendar
Don't miss a single day
reflection: How did your energy change over the 7 days?

title: Create something with your hands
description: A drawing, a sculpture, a photo taken with intention. The process matters, not the result.
proof_prompt: Photo of what you created.
steps: Choose your material
Make it without judging
Enjoy the process
reflection: What did you express without realizing it?

title: Write a letter to your future self
description: Write to the person you'll be in 1 year. Tell them what you hope for, what you fear, what you're learning.
proof_prompt: Paste the letter or a fragment of it.
steps: Find 20 minutes of quiet
Write without editing
Seal it and keep it for 1 year
reflection: What would you most want to know one year from now?

title: Photograph the beauty of the ordinary
description: Walk for 30 minutes and photograph ordinary things that have something special about them.
proof_prompt: Post your most beautiful photo.
steps: Head out with no set destination
Look as if you were seeing everything for the first time
Photograph whatever catches your eye
reflection: What did you notice that usually goes unseen?

title: A meal cooked with intention
description: Cook something from scratch, without rushing. Be present in every step.
proof_prompt: Photo of the finished meal.
steps: Choose a new recipe
Buy the ingredients mindfully
Cook with no phone or TV
reflection: How was it to be fully present in the kitchen?

title: Call someone you love for no reason
description: Not a text — a real call. Talk without rushing.
proof_prompt: Write how that conversation went.
steps: Think of someone you haven't talked to in a while
Call with no particular purpose
Be present in the conversation
reflection: What connection did you feel?

title: 30 minutes in nature — no phone
description: Go outside and leave your phone at home. Observe. Listen. Just be.
proof_prompt: Write what you observed, heard, or felt.
steps: Leave your phone at home
Walk with no destination
Observe with all your senses
reflection: When did you last feel fully present in nature?

title: A letter of forgiveness to yourself
description: Write yourself a letter of forgiveness for something from the past that you still carry.
proof_prompt: Write a fragment or how you felt writing it.
steps: Choose something from the past you haven't forgiven yourself for
Write as if you were writing to a friend
Read it with kindness
reflection: What changed in you after you wrote it?

title: 3 things I accept about myself
description: Not your strengths — things you see as flaws and choose to accept.
proof_prompt: Write the 3 things and why you choose to accept them.
steps: Sit with yourself in silence for 5 minutes
Write without judging
Read it out loud
reflection: How did it feel to say these things with kindness?

title: Do an unexpected gesture for a stranger
description: Buy a coffee, hold the door, say something kind. Without hoping for anything in return.
proof_prompt: Tell what happened and how you felt.
steps: Stay attentive to those around you today
Choose a small but sincere gesture
Do it without mentioning it to anyone else
reflection: What did you feel giving without expecting anything?

title: Truly listen to someone
description: Find someone who needs to be heard. Don't give advice. Just listen.
proof_prompt: How was it to listen without stepping in?
steps: Choose someone who seems to have something on their mind
Ask how they are and listen
Resist the urge to offer solutions
reflection: What did you learn about this person that you didn't know?

title: What values guide your life?
description: Write the first 5 values without overthinking. Ask yourself: are you living by them?
proof_prompt: Write the values and a reflection on how present they are.
steps: Write 5 values in 2 minutes
Don't edit, don't overthink
Reflect: which one is most neglected?
reflection: If your life were a film, which value would be the central theme?

title: What makes you happy?
description: Not what should make you happy. What makes YOU happy.
proof_prompt: List 10 things and choose the most important one.
steps: Quickly write 10 things that bring you joy
Don't censor anything
Ask yourself: how many of them do you do regularly?
reflection: How often do you allow yourself to do what makes you happy?

title: Try something you've never done before
description: Step out of your comfort zone, gently. Give it at least 30 minutes.
proof_prompt: Photo during or after the activity.
steps: Choose something completely new
Give it at least 30 minutes
Don't judge yourself if you're not good at it the first time
reflection: Did you feel you discovered something about yourself?

title: Revive an abandoned hobby
description: Something you once loved and let slip away. Bring it back to life for a day.
proof_prompt: Any proof — photo, text, video.
steps: Think about what you loved as a child
Set aside 1h for that hobby
Notice how you feel coming back to it
reflection: Why did you abandon it? What brought it back?

title: Check in with yourself
description: How are you today — really? 2 minutes of honesty with yourself.
proof_prompt: Write a word or a sentence about how you are today.
steps: Sit with yourself for 2 minutes
Be completely honest
There is no wrong answer

title: 3 things you're grateful for
description: Not something generic — something specific from today.
proof_prompt: Write the 3 things.
steps: Think about today
Choose 3 concrete, specific things
Write them down

title: The first hour is yours
description: Wake up 1 hour earlier. No phone. No news. No social media. This hour belongs to you before it belongs to the world.
proof_prompt: Write 3 words about how you feel in this hour of yours. Nothing more.
steps: Set your alarm 1 hour earlier
Keep your phone on airplane mode until 9:00
Be present in the quiet of the morning
Write the 3 words at the end of the hour
reflection: What did you discover about yourself in the quiet of the morning?

title: Your body speaks
description: 5 minutes of movement when you wake up. It doesn't have to be intense. Stretching, dancing, walking around the house. Your body knows what it needs.
proof_prompt: Photograph the place where you moved. Not yourself — the place. The morning light.
steps: Right after waking, before anything else
Put on a song that makes you move
5 minutes of mindful movement
Photograph the place at the end
reflection: What did your body tell you in these 5 minutes?

title: Intention of the day
description: Write ONE single thing you want to FEEL today. Not to do. Not to achieve. To FEEL.
proof_prompt: Write ONE single word or a short sentence — your intention for today.
steps: Sit in silence for 2 minutes
Ask yourself: what do I want to FEEL today?
Write the first answer that comes — don't analyze
Read it out loud
reflection: In the evening — did you feel it? Why or why not?

title: Coffee in silence
description: Drink your first coffee or tea with no phone, no news, no music. 10 minutes of complete presence with your drink.
proof_prompt: Photograph your cup. No filters. Natural light.
steps: Prepare your favorite drink
Leave your phone in another room
Sit for 10 minutes with just your thoughts
Photograph the cup at the end
reflection: What thoughts came up in the silence?

title: Today's letter
description: Write 5 sentences about how you want today to go — as if it had already happened perfectly.
proof_prompt: The 5 sentences. In the past tense, as if the day had been perfect.
steps: Close your eyes for 1 minute
Imagine the best version of your day
Write 5 sentences in the past tense: "Today I felt..."
Read them out loud before you leave the house
reflection: In the evening: how many of the 5 sentences came true?

title: Concrete gratitude
description: Not "I'm grateful for my family". Choose ONE specific moment from yesterday. A small, concrete detail.
proof_prompt: Describe the specific moment. Where were you? What happened? How exactly did you feel?
steps: Think about yesterday
Identify ONE small but real moment
Describe it in detail — not generically
Feel gratitude for that moment
reflection: Why did you choose exactly this moment?

title: Breathing
description: The 4-7-8 technique: inhale for 4 seconds, hold for 7 seconds, exhale for 8 seconds. Repeat 4 times.
proof_prompt: Describe your state BEFORE and your state AFTER.
steps: Sit comfortably with your back straight
Inhale through your nose for 4 seconds
Hold your breath for 7 seconds
Exhale through your mouth for 8 seconds
Repeat 4 times
reflection: What changed in your body and mind?

title: Vision of the day
description: Close your eyes for 2 minutes. Imagine the best version of today. Then draw or write what you saw.
proof_prompt: Draw or write your vision. Any form. Any color. Don't judge.
steps: Sit comfortably and close your eyes
Let your mind picture the perfect day
Notice the details — colors, sounds, emotions
Open your eyes and put it on paper or in text right away
reflection: Which element of the vision surprised you?

title: One thing that would make me proud
description: Not the to-do list. ONE single thing. If you do only this today — the day is a complete success.
proof_prompt: In the morning: write that one thing. In the evening: how did you feel after doing it?
steps: In the morning: identify ONE single important thing
Write it somewhere visible — on a note beside you
Do that thing first, before anything else
In the evening: report how you felt
reflection: Why does this thing truly matter?

title: My mantra for today
description: A single sentence to guide you today. Not a quote. Yours. From what you feel right now, in this moment.
proof_prompt: Your mantra. One sentence. Yours.
steps: Sit with yourself for 1 minute
What do you need to hear today?
Write the sentence — yours, not a quote
Repeat it 3 times out loud
reflection: Did this mantra help you today?

title: A letter of forgiveness to yourself
description: The hardest thing you haven't forgiven yourself for. Write yourself a letter as if you were writing to a dear friend who made a mistake.
proof_prompt: Your letter. Complete or fragmented. Mara judges nothing.
steps: Find 30 minutes of complete solitude
Identify that thing you haven't forgiven yourself for
Write as if writing to a friend — with kindness
Read it out loud, alone
reflection: What changed after you wrote it?

title: Your greatest fear
description: Write or draw about your greatest fear. Don't analyze it. Don't justify it. Just describe it.
proof_prompt: Text or drawing — whichever feels easier for expressing what you feel.
steps: Sit with your fear for 5 minutes without running from it
Notice where you feel it in your body
Describe it or draw it without judging
Give it a name
reflection: What happened when you stood face to face with it?

title: Who hurt you the most?
description: Not to judge or take revenge. To understand and free yourself. Write without editing.
proof_prompt: Write freely. Don't edit. Don't censor. Mara reads with complete empathy.
steps: Make sure you're alone and safe
Write without lifting your pen/hands from the keyboard
Don't edit, don't censor, don't judge
At the end, take 3 deep breaths
reflection: What did you feel after you wrote it?

title: The child within you
description: What would you say to the 7-year-old you once were? What would they want to know? What would make them feel safe?
proof_prompt: A letter to your younger self. Or a drawing. Or both.
steps: Find a photo of yourself as a child if you have one
Look at it for a few minutes
Write them a letter or draw for them
What would you have wanted to hear back then?
reflection: What did that child feel when they read your letter?

title: Your mask
description: What face do you show the world vs who you really are when no one is watching? Describe the difference honestly.
proof_prompt: Text or two drawings: the mask and the real face.
steps: Think about the last week
How did you present yourself to others?
Who were you when you were alone?
Describe or draw both versions
reflection: How big is the difference? Why?

title: The voice in your head
description: How do you talk to yourself when no one is listening? With kindness or with cruelty? Write 10 things you regularly tell yourself.
proof_prompt: 10 things you tell yourself. Honestly. Exactly as they are.
steps: Be completely honest — no one else is reading
Write the first 10 recurring thoughts you have about yourself
Mark each: kind or harsh?
Choose ONE harsh thought and rewrite it with kindness
reflection: If someone spoke to a friend the way you speak to yourself — how would you feel?

title: Your boundaries
description: Where do you say YES when you want to say NO? With whom? When? Why do you keep giving in?
proof_prompt: 3 concrete situations where you said YES when you wanted to say NO.
steps: Think about the last month
Identify 3 real, concrete situations
For each: what you said vs what you wanted to say
Choose one and write how it would have looked if you'd said NO
reflection: Why is it hard for you to say NO in those situations?

title: Your relationship with money
description: Not about how much you have or don't have. About WHAT YOU FEEL toward money. Fear? Shame? Power? Indifference?
proof_prompt: Write honestly about your relationship with money. Childhood, family, beliefs.
steps: Think about your first memory involving money
What did your parents say about money?
What do you feel now when you think about money?
Where do you think this emotion comes from?
reflection: What belief about money do you want to change?

title: Your body — a letter
description: Write a letter to your body. What would you tell it? What does it tell you? What would you thank it for? What would you apologize for?
proof_prompt: Your letter to your body. Complete, honest, from the heart.
steps: Sit in silence for a few minutes
Do a mental scan from head to toe
What do you feel in each part of your body?
Write the letter — with gratitude and forgiveness
reflection: What did your body tell you in this letter?

title: The moment that changed you
description: An event that changed everything. There's a before and an after. Describe both.
proof_prompt: The story of the moment. Before. The event. After. Who you are now because of it.
steps: Identify that moment — you know which one it is
Describe who you were before
Describe what happened
Describe who you are now because of it
reflection: If that moment hadn't happened — who would you be today?

title: What does success mean to YOU?
description: Not for your parents. Not for society. Not for your friends. For you. Now. Real.
proof_prompt: Define your success. With no social filter.
steps: Completely ignore what others think
Write your own definition of success
Is it about money? Time? Relationships? Freedom? Creativity?
Are you living by this definition now?
reflection: How far are you from your real success?

title: Your deepest longing
description: What do you long for most? Not necessarily something material. It can be a state, a connection, a version of yourself.
proof_prompt: Text or drawing — whichever better expresses that longing.
steps: Sit in complete silence for 5 minutes
What do you feel is truly missing?
Don't analyze — feel it
Express that longing without censoring
reflection: How long has this longing existed? What creates it?

title: A letter to your future self
description: Write a letter to yourself 5 years from now. What do you want them to know? What do you hope for? What do you leave them as a legacy?
proof_prompt: Dear me, 5 years from now...
steps: Imagine you are yourself in 5 years
Write them an honest letter
Tell them what you hope for, what you fear, what you want for them
Seal it in the app
reflection: What surprised you in what you wrote?

title: Gratitude for adversity
description: The hardest moment of your life. Not the easiest — the HARDEST. What did it teach you?
proof_prompt: The moment. What it taught you. Who you are because of it.
steps: Identify the hardest moment — you know which one it is
Write what happened without dramatizing
Identify 3 things you gained from that moment
Give thanks to that moment
reflection: If that moment hadn't happened — what wouldn't you have known?

title: Who are you, really?
description: Not what you do. Not what you have. Not the role you play. Who are you? This question has no wrong answer.
proof_prompt: Text, drawing, photo collage — anything that expresses who you really are.
steps: Sit in complete silence for 10 minutes
Ask yourself: who am I?
Don't look for the "correct" answer — there isn't one
Express what you feel, not what you think
reflection: How has the answer changed compared to a year ago?

title: Photograph your day
description: A single photo to represent how you feel today. Not perfect. Not filtered. Authentic.
proof_prompt: Your photo of today. It can be anything.
steps: Don't rush — look for the right moment
Photograph without a filter and without editing
It can be an object, a place, a light, a shadow
It should represent how you feel — not how you look
reflection: Why does this image represent your day?

title: Draw your fear
description: You don't have to be an artist. Any shape, any color. Give your fear a visual form.
proof_prompt: A photo of your drawing. No matter how "unprofessional" it is.
steps: Take a blank sheet and drawing tools
Don't plan — let your hand go
Draw what your fear looks like
Give it a title
reflection: What does your fear look like? What surprised you?

title: Write a letter to a stranger
description: Someone you don't know but sense needs these words. Maybe it's someone going through what you went through.
proof_prompt: The complete letter. It can be published anonymously in the community.
steps: Think about a hard moment in your life
What would you have wanted to hear back then?
Write for that unknown person
You can choose whether to publish it anonymously or keep it
reflection: Writing for someone else — what did you discover about yourself?

title: The collage of your dream
description: Find 5 images around you — not from magazines — that represent your ideal life. Photograph them together.
proof_prompt: A photo of your collage. Or 5 separate photos.
steps: Search your home or your surroundings
Find 5 objects or images that represent your dream
Arrange them and photograph
Write 2 words for each
reflection: What did you discover truly matters?

title: The music of your moment
description: A song that represents exactly what you feel right now. Not what you like — what you FEEL. Why this song?
proof_prompt: The song title and why it represents exactly what you feel now.
steps: Sit in silence for 2 minutes
What song comes to mind spontaneously?
Listen to it once, all the way through
Write why this song represents today
reflection: What does your music choice say about your state?

title: Write a 4-line poem
description: It doesn't have to rhyme. It doesn't have to be perfect. 4 lines about today, about you, about what you feel.
proof_prompt: Your poem. 4 lines. Yours.
steps: Don't think — write the first thing that comes
Don't edit after you've written it
Don't judge whether it's "good" or not
Read it out loud
reflection: What surprised you in your own poem?

title: Photograph ordinary beauty
description: Go out for 30 minutes with no destination. Photograph 5 ordinary things that have something special about them.
proof_prompt: The best 1-3 photos from your walk.
steps: Head out with no destination and no rush
Look as if you were seeing everything for the first time
Photograph whatever catches your eye
No filters, no editing
reflection: What did you see today that usually goes unseen?

title: Write the beginning of your book
description: The first page of the book about your life. Not the biography — the book. The first paragraph. Wherever you want it to begin.
proof_prompt: The first paragraph. You can write in any person, from any moment of your life.
steps: Don't plan — write the first thing that comes
It can start anywhere — childhood, yesterday, now
Write without editing the first time
Read it and decide whether to keep it or rewrite it
reflection: Why did you choose to start there?

title: Draw where you want to be
description: Visualization through art. The place, the people, what your ideal life looks like. Not perfect — real.
proof_prompt: A photo of your drawing or collage.
steps: Take a large sheet if you have one
Draw or paste images
Include: the place, the people, the activities, the emotions
Don't judge — express
reflection: Which element of the drawing is the most important?

title: The letter you never sent
description: To someone from your past or present. Everything you wanted to say and didn't. Now you can.
proof_prompt: The complete letter. You decide: send it, keep it, or delete it.
steps: Identify the person and what you wanted to say
Write without thinking about whether you'll send it
At the end you have 3 options: send, keep private, delete
Whichever you choose — it's your decision
reflection: What changed after you wrote it?

title: Photograph your hands
description: What do your hands tell? What have they built? What have they destroyed? What have they healed? What have they created?
proof_prompt: A photo of your hands + a few words about their story.
steps: Look at your hands for a few minutes
Think about everything they've done
Photograph them in natural light
Write 3 sentences about their story
reflection: What did you discover about yourself looking at your hands?

title: Redraw your bad day
description: Take your most recent bad day. Draw or write how it would have looked if it had gone well.
proof_prompt: The redrawn day — text or drawing.
steps: Think about a recent bad day
Describe what went wrong
Rewrite or redraw how it could have been
What should have been different?
reflection: What can you actually control about a bad day?

title: Your manifesto
description: 5 things you believe with your whole being. The principles you live by or want to live by.
proof_prompt: Your manifesto. 5 principles. Yours.
steps: Don't overthink — write what comes
What is non-negotiable for you?
How do you want to live?
What do you want to stand for?
reflection: Are you living by this manifesto now?

title: Say it out loud
description: Say out loud something you've never said before. You don't have to record it — you have to SAY it.
proof_prompt: Not what you said — but how you felt when you said it. And whether the world changed.
steps: Identify that unspoken thing
Find a private place
Say it out loud — 3 times
Sit for a few minutes with what you feel afterward
reflection: Why haven't you said it until now?

title: Create something with your hands
description: Anything — clay, paper, wood, food, fabric. Something that didn't exist before you made it.
proof_prompt: A photo of your creation. Its story in 2 sentences.
steps: Choose a material from around the house
Don't plan — let your hands go
Make something — anything
Photograph it before judging the result
reflection: What did you feel while you were creating?

title: The résumé of your real life
description: Not the jobs. The moments that defined you. 5 experiences that truly mattered in shaping you.
proof_prompt: The 5 defining experiences. Not jobs — life moments.
steps: Think about the experiences that changed you
Choose 5 — not necessarily positive ones
Describe what you gained from each
This is your real experience
reflection: What pattern do you notice in these 5 experiences?

title: What would the brave version of you do?
description: A decision you keep putting off. What would your version with no fear, no excuses, no "but" do?
proof_prompt: The postponed decision. What the brave version would do. The first small step you can take tomorrow.
steps: Identify the postponed decision — you know which one it is
Write: what would your fearless version do?
Identify the smallest possible step
Commit to Mara that you'll take it tomorrow
reflection: What is really holding you back?

title: A day in your ideal life
description: Describe in detail a perfect day from your future. From waking up to going to sleep. Concrete and specific.
proof_prompt: Your ideal day. Hour by hour. Concrete.
steps: Write from 06:00 to 23:00
Be specific — not "I wake up happy"
Include: where you are, with whom, what you do, how you feel
Don't censor anything you desire
reflection: Which element of this day can you start building now?

title: The skill that scares you
description: What skill have you avoided learning? Why does it scare you? It can be anything — coding, painting, dancing, public speaking.
proof_prompt: The skill. Why it scares you. A first small step you can take today.
steps: Identify the skill you think about but never start
Write why it truly scares you
Find the smallest possible step
Take that step — today, right now
reflection: What would change in your life if you mastered that skill?

title: The difficult conversation
description: A conversation you've been avoiding for a long time. With whom? About what? Mara prepares you for it.
proof_prompt: With whom. About what. What exactly you want to say. What you fear will happen.
steps: Identify the avoided conversation
Write exactly what you want to say
Write what you fear the other person will say
Role-play it with Mara beforehand
reflection: What would change if you had this conversation?

title: Money and your dream
description: How much does your ideal life cost? Calculate it for real. Monthly. Yearly. Without scaring yourself.
proof_prompt: The real calculation. The ideal life. How much it costs monthly and yearly.
steps: Take the ideal life you described
Estimate the real monthly cost
Calculate the gap versus your current income
Identify 3 ways to close the gap
reflection: Is it more or less than you thought?

title: The career change
description: If you could do something else tomorrow — what would it be? Mara helps you explore the real possibility.
proof_prompt: What you would do. Why you don't do it now. What would need to change.
steps: Write: if there were no risks, what would you do?
Actually research that career — 30 minutes
Write what you'd gain and what you'd lose
Identify ONE small step toward it
reflection: What keeps you in your current place more — security or fear?

title: Your relationship with time
description: Track a whole day — exactly what you did, hour by hour. Honestly. Without embellishing.
proof_prompt: The day's time journal. Hour by hour. Honest.
steps: In the morning: set a reminder every 2 hours
Note exactly what you did
At the end: calculate the % of time per activity
Identify your biggest "time killer"
reflection: What did this day show you about your real priorities?

title: Ask for help
description: Call or write to someone and ask for help with something real. Not metaphorical. Something concrete you can't do alone.
proof_prompt: Who you talked to. What you asked for. How you felt asking. What happened after.
steps: Identify something you truly need help with
Choose a person who can help
Ask directly — without excessive apologies
Report honestly what happened
reflection: Why was it hard or easy for you to ask?

title: The first step
description: That thing you've been putting off for months or years. Today you take the FIRST STEP. However small. Impossible to make smaller.
proof_prompt: What the thing is. What step you took exactly. How small it was. How you felt after.
steps: Identify the postponed thing — you know which one it is
Identify the smallest possible step
Do it now — while you're reading this
Report exactly what you did
reflection: How did you feel after the first step?
